1. Heard Sri Shyam Babu Vaish, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Mayank Awasthi, learned Brief Holder for the State and perused the record.
2.

6000377 of 2020, State v. Ravindra Mohan Pandey and others, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506,

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that a first information report has been lodged by opposite party no.2 against 7 person including the applicant on 21.03.2020 at 16:40 hrs.
bearing Case Crime No. 41 of 2020, with the allegation that marriage of opposite party no. 2 was solemnized with Ravindra Mohan Pandey on 25.11.2013.
After marriage she was harassed by family members for additional dowry demand.
There is allegation of misbehavior with opposite party no. 2 by the applicant.
After investigation charge sheet has been submitted.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is Jeth of opposite party no. 2 and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He is a Government employee who works as a peon in the office of A.D.O. Panchayat at Sonbhadra and the opposite party no. 2 was not staying with him.
He further submits that after lodging of the FIR, there was some understanding between the parties, therefore, opposite party no. 2 started to stay along with her husband.
However, the matter could not be settled between them.
It is further contended that the applicant has never demanded any dowry nor he ever physically or mentally harassed opposite party no. 2.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate falsity of the allegations made against him.
Allegations as levelled against the applicant are false hence the proceedings may be quashed.

5. Learned A.G.A. on the other hand submits that from the version of FIR as well as statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it is clear that the applicant has misbehaved with O.P. No. 2 as there is specific allegation against him in this regard.
He further submits that all the contentions raised by the applicant's counsel relate to disputed questions of fact.

On the basis of material on record after conducting of statutory investigation under Chapter XII Cr.P.C. by the investigating officer, a strong prima facie case is made out against the applicant for the commission of the alleged incident.
6. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the records of the present application.

7. This Court finds that the submissions made by the applicant's learned counsel call for adjudication on pure questions of fact which may adequately be adjudicated upon only by the trial court and while doing so even the submissions made on points of law can also be more appropriately gone into by the trial court in this case.

The issue whether it is appropriate for this Court being the highest Court to exercise its jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash the charge-sheet and the proceedings at the stage when the Magistrate has merely issued process against the applicant and trial is yet to come only on the submission made by the learned counsel for the applicant that present criminal case initiated by opposite party no.2 are not only malicious but also abuse of process of law has elaborately been discussed by the Apex Court in the following judgments:-
(i) R.P. Kapur Versus State of Punjab; AIR 1960 SC 866,
(ii) State of Haryana & Ors. Versus Ch. Bhajan Lal & Ors.;1992 Supp.(1) SCC 335,
(iii) State of Bihar & Anr. Versus P.P. Sharma & Anr.; 1992 Supp (1) SCC 222,

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, this Court does not deem it proper, and therefore cannot be persuaded to have a pre-trial before the actual trial begins.

A threadbare discussion of various facts and circumstances, as they emerge from the allegations made against the accused, is being purposely avoided by the Court for the reason, lest the same might cause any prejudice to either side during trial.

But it shall suffice to observe that the perusal of the F.I.R. and the material collected by the Investigating Officer on the basis of which the charge sheet has been submitted makes out a prima facie case against the accused at this stage and there appear to be sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

I do not find any justification to quash the charge sheet or the proceedings against the applicant arising out of them as the case does not fall in any of the categories recognized by the Apex Court which may justify their quashing.

9. The prayer for quashing the impugned charge-sheet dated 24.09.2020 and cognizance order dated 12.02.2021 as well as the entire proceedings of the aforesaid case are refused, as I do not see any abuse of the court's process at this pre-trial stage.
10. The present application has no merit and is, accordingly, rejected.
